assertion_analysis.tests/standard_names/test_campaign.py:75: fails if the runner stops taking its pre-drain read before clear_quarantine, because the expected event list begins with fetch:a; it does not fail on what that read is used for.
assertion_analysis.tests/standard_names/test_campaign_conve: fails if _split_name_accepted stops excluding a reviewed member (eligible would hold all four ids); it does not fail if measure_batch's drift comparison is removed, because the batch it hands over holds only accepted names.
fails if the drift clause is deleted, but not if the prior_rows comparison is removed: its post-drain stage (reviewed) is not accepted, so the unrepaired absolute check reports the same drift.

fails if any score-based acceptance is reintroduced, because accepted would read 2 and the literal 50.00% (1/2 touched) halt string would not be produced; logs-pinned-truth-mutation.log records that mutation reddening this test alone.
fails if the comparison reverts to the absolute post-drain stage check at campaign.py:655-669; logs-drift-guard-mutation.log records exactly that reinstatement reddening this test alone.
does not fail for any defect in the code it names: the expected value re-spells the plan the test itself supplied, so a planning path that stopped producing skipped members leaves it green.

blocking: the two-arm gate table states base `4 failed, 230 passed` with `the three new tests` and head `233 passed`, but logs-gate-base.log records `6 failed, 230 passed` naming all five ids in tests/standard_names/test_campaign_convergence_gate.py, and five tests failing at base with one residual failure at head gives 235 passed; the table is a leftover from the three-test revision (commit 6a52f5140) and contradicts the fragment's own sentence at line 205 that all five fail against main.

non-blocking: the sentence says `A name with no inherited row, or absent from the post-drain read, is still drift`, but campaign.py:655-669 reports drift only for an id missing from the post-drain read; an id with no prior row whose post-drain stage is not accepted falls through to the `continue` at campaign.py:666 and is skipped, so the fragment states a stricter rule than the gate implements.

non-blocking: test_apply_reports_each_skipped_member_with_its_stage asserts summary["skipped"] against the same entries the test itself hand-wrote into the plan it passes to apply_families, so the assertion holds for any function that re-spells its input; and no test anywhere exercises plan_family_applies producing a skipped entry (docs_eligible and skipped appear only in this file, and the fake graphs in tests/standard_names/test_harmonize_anchor_pin.py return [] from query so _name_stages always answers empty), leaving the brief's `exclude it at planning` guarded only by the private-helper test at :108.

non-blocking: _NAME_STAGE_QUERY and _name_stages duplicate the by-ids name_stage read that campaign.py:711-731 already owns (_REFRESH_QUERY / default_fetch_refreshed); the same result is one dict comprehension over the owner's rows and harmonize already imports campaign lazily at :1243 and :1721, so this is a second query rather than an extension of the owner.
